newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: NWE bunkers nudge higher, Med ports up sharply.
newsitem.headline: NWE bunkers nudge higher, Med ports up sharply.

text.p: European bunkers firmed on Monday, in northwest Europe by about $1 a tonne and in certain Mediterranean ports by $2 or more, deterring all but the most desperate of buyers, dealers said.
Rotterdam 380 CST fuel oil traded in the range $122/$124 fob, up about $1 on Friday's close. Barge trade was reasonably heavy, but bunker trading failed to ignite.
"We've seen a couple of thousand tonnes traded. That's it," one bunker trader said.
Hamburg prices followed Rotterdam's lead, up another $1 to around $130 delivered. As in Rotterdam, trading was slack.

Prices in a number of Mediterranean ports rose sharply. Fos and Algeciras were up $3 a tonne, but Augusta and Piraeus were steady. Firm prices continued to keep buyers away for all but the most urgent purchases.
Prices in the Middle East and Africa also rose, despite modest weakness in Singapore.
Egyptian prices were up about $3 a tonne, killing most enquiries. Fujairah was up $1 with traders indicating supplies were tight.
Durban 180 CST was up $1 a tonne to $126/$128 ex wharf.
